newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks lower at midday.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks lower at midday.

text.p: Wall Street stocks were lower at midday Tuesday as investors sifted through economic data to get some clue as to whether the Fed will raise rates when its policy-making FOMC meets next week.
The Dow industrials were down 17 points at 6938 while declines led advances by 14 to eight on volume of about 201 million shares.
"The big worry is that we are shifting into overdrive, entering a boom/bust trajectory," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment strategist at First Albany Corp.
"That means that the economy gets too strong, the Fed is required to cool it by raising interest rates and invariably they raise rates too high and a recession follows," he said.
February housing starts released this morning were higher than expected, and Johnson said, gave the Fed more ammunition to with which to justify a rate hike.

"The question is much deeper than just whether the Fed will raise rates on March 25," Johnson said. "The worry is that the economy is starting to accelerate and that a rate increase will be the first in a series which lead to the end of the bull market and the economic expansion."
Housing starts rose by 12.2 percent to an annualized rate of 1.528 million compared to a revised reading of 1.362 million in January.
"That was one heck of an increase," an analyst said. "But my guess is that Fed would like the luxury of two more months of employment data to find support for a rate hike."
The Nasdaq Composite Index, a barometer of the high tech stocks, was down 5.33 points at 1274 while the Standard & Poor's 500 Index was down 3.77 to 791.94.
Analysts also said that investors were being cautious ahead of tomorrow's February consumer price index.
Ken Tower, technical analyst at UST Securities, said the market was in a corrective phase and holding up well.

"We are nicely surprised that the Dow has been able to hold at the 6850 level," he said. "Our concern was that it would not hold this first support level and trade down to to 6650 level, which is the next one down.
"We are not looking for a major decline in the stock market. This is a correction at the end of the rally which began last July," he said.
Micron Technology Inc was the most actively traded NYSE issue. The stock was down 3-1/4 at 40-3/8 after the company reported second quarter earnings.
Harman International Industries Inc shares were down 11-3/4 at 34-1/4, a day after the maker of high-fidelity audio products warned of a drop in third quarter profits.
First Chicago NBD Corp told analysts the company will earn less in its credit card business in 1997 than the $347 million after-tax net income recorded in 1996. Shares fell 2-5/8 to 55-3/4.
